To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the police’s legitimacy is based on the combination of the duty to obey the police and the belief that the police share a common moral purpose with citizens; and 2) the police’s moral purpose is a key factor in the public’s willingness to comply with the police’s instructions.

the more people believe that the police act according to the law and in a way that is consistent with their moral values, the more willing they are to comply with police directives and the more likely they are to accept police authority

people accept the right of legal institutions to dictate appropriate behaviour when: 1) they recognize the power and authority of the institution, and 2) they believe the institution acts according the shared moral purposes of citizens and the institution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of why do people obey the law.
why people obey the law and how the law can influence behaviour.
the question of why do people comply with the law? We are particularly interested in the influence of the police on public compliance with the criminal law.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
legitimacy is the acceptance of an institution’s right to dictate behaviour and the belief in the institution’s shared moral purpose.
legitimacy is the perception that the law is both morally correct and procedurally just.
people comply with the law because they believe the institution that is enacting it to be legitimate, and that they feel a duty and a willingness to obey.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the police’s legitimacy depends not only on their ability to enforce their authority, but also on their ability to justify their authority.
people are more likely to follow the law when they believe that it is legitimate.

legitimacy is not simply the acceptance of power but also its justification.
